objetivo: That the student recognizes sources of light, understands that light travels in a straight line, understands that a shadow forms when an opaque object blocks the light, and notices that the size of the shadow changes depending on the position of the source.
hatsumon: Why is your shadow long in the afternoon and short at noon?

turnos.utterance_formal: Good morning. Come over to the window for a second: do you see that dark shape on the floor, the one that moves when I move?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, good morning. Come over to the window a sec: you see that dark shape on the floor? The one that moves when I move?

turnos.utterance_formal: Back to your seats now, and get out your notebook.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, back to your seats now, get your notebook out.

turnos.utterance_formal: Think about this: why is your shadow long in the afternoon and short at noon?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, think about it: why is your shadow long in the afternoon and short at noon?

turnos.utterance_formal: Hold on to your answer; we'll answer it at the end.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Hold on to your answer; we'll answer it at the end.

turnos.utterance_formal: To be able to see anything, we first need light.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: To be able to see anything, we first need light.

operations.text: Light sources
To see we need **light**

turnos.utterance_formal: Light comes from certain places we call light sources.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Light comes from certain places we call light sources.

set.text: To see we need **light**. Light comes from places called **light sources**.

turnos.utterance_formal: The biggest light source we have is the Sun.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The biggest light source we have is the Sun.

turnos.utterance_formal: But there's more: fire, a lamp, a candle... they all give off light.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: But there's more: fire, a lamp, a candle... they all give off light.

fire
a lamp

turnos.utterance_formal: Here's a lamp, which is also a light source.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Here's a lamb, which is also a light source.

turnos.utterance_formal: The Moon doesn't count: it doesn't make its own light, it only reflects the Sun's.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The Moon doesn't count: it doesn't make its own light, it only reflects the Sun's.

operations.text: The Moon is not a light source: it only reflects the Sun's light.

turnos.utterance_formal: Something important about light: it always travels in a straight line.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Something important about light: it always travels in a straight line.

operations.text: Light and Shadow
Light travels in a straight line
Light leaves the source and goes **straight**

turnos.utterance_formal: Light leaves the Sun along straight lines, never curved.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Light leaves the Sun along straight lines, never crooked.

turnos.utterance_formal: Those straight lines that come out of the Sun are called rays.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Those straight lines that come out of the Sun are called rays, ok?

operations.text: rays

turnos.utterance_formal: That's why we can't see behind a wall: light doesn't bend around it.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's why we can't see behind a wall: light doesn't bend around it.

operations.text: We can't see behind a wall because light doesn't bend around it.

turnos.utterance_formal: So far we've covered where light comes from and how it travels.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So far we've covered where light comes from and how it travels.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now then, shadow: it forms when an object blocks the path of light.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now then, shadow: it forms when an object blocks the path of light.

operations.text: What is a shadow?
**Shadow** forms when an object **blocks** the light

turnos.utterance_formal: If you stand in the sun, your body blocks the light and your shadow is left behind you.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: If you stand in the sun, your body blocks the light and your shadow is left behind you.

turnos.utterance_formal: Notice that the shadow comes out on the opposite side from the light.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Notice that the shadow comes out on the op posite side from the light.

operations.text: The shadow comes out on the opposite side from the light.

turnos.utterance_formal: Same with a tree: its shadow falls on the opposite side from the Sun.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Same with a tree: its shadow falls on the opposite side from the Sun.

turnos.utterance_formal: Have you noticed your shadow always copies you? Wherever you go, it goes with you.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Have you noticed your shadow always copies you? Wherever you go, it goes with you.

turnos.utterance_formal: Pay close attention to how a shadow forms, that's the central idea.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Pay close attention to how a shadow forms, that's the central idea.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now, a shadow isn't always the same size: its size changes.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now, a shadow isn't always the same size: its size changes.

operations.text: The size of the shadow
Shadow **size** changes depending on where the light is

turnos.utterance_formal: At noon the Sun is way up high, and the shadow stays short.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: At noon the Sun is way up high, and the shadow stays short.

set.text: Shadow **size** changes depending on where the light is: at noon the Sun is up high, so the shadow is short

turnos.utterance_formal: In the afternoon the Sun looks low, and the shadow stretches out long.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: In the after noon the Sun looks low, and the shadow stretches out long.

set.text: Shadow **size** changes depending on where the light is: at noon the Sun is up high, so the shadow is short; in the afternoon the Sun is low, so the shadow is long.

turnos.utterance_formal: Look at a pole at noon: it barely has a short little shadow underneath.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Look at a pole at noon: it barely has a short little shadow underneath.

turnos.utterance_formal: Can you imagine why sometimes your shadow is taller than you?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Can you imagine why sometimes your shadow is taller than you?

turnos.utterance_formal: So, your shadow is long in the afternoon because the Sun is low.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So, your shadow is long in the afternoon because the Sun is low.

operations.text: Your shadow is long in the **afternoon** because the Sun is low.

turnos.utterance_formal: Go back and look at the question from the beginning: it's already answered.

turnos.utterance_formal: One more thing: not all materials make shadows the same way.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: One more thing: not all materials make shadows the same way.

turnos.utterance_formal: It depends on whether the material lets light through or not.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: It depends on whether the material lets light through or not.

operations.text: Not everything makes the same shadow
Shadow depends on the **material**

turnos.utterance_formal: Opaque materials don't let light through and they make a dark shadow.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The o paque materials don't let light through and they make a dark shadow.

set.text: Shadow depends on the **material**: **opaque** materials don't let light through, so they make a dark shadow

turnos.utterance_formal: Transparent materials, like glass, let the light through, almost all of it.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The trans parent materials, like glass, let the light through, almost all of it.

set.text: Shadow depends on the **material**: **opaque** materials don't let light through, so they make a dark shadow; **transparent** materials, like glass, let the light through.

turnos.utterance_formal: Look at a sheet of glass: light passes through it and it barely makes a shadow.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Look at a sheet of glass: light passes through it and it barely makes a shadow.

turnos.utterance_formal: That's why glass windows let us see the yard, light and all.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's why glass windows let us see the yard, light and all.

operations.text: Glass windows let us see the yard, light and all.

turnos.utterance_formal: Notice what decides whether something makes a shadow or not: the material.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Notice what decides whether something makes a shadow or not: the material.

turnos.utterance_formal: Hold on to today's big idea, the one that sums everything up.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Hold on to that big idea for today, the one that wraps it all up.

operations.text: Light travels in straight lines, so an object in its way leaves a shadow.

turnos.utterance_formal: And with that: a shadow forms when an opaque object blocks the light.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And with that: a shadow forms when an opaque object blocks the light.

turnos.utterance_formal: And today's big word, the one you shouldn't forget, is shadow.

turnos.utterance_formal: Remember how light travels: always in a straight line.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Remember how light travels: always in a straight line.
